gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Audio Science Review's bench test (amirm, 2020-07-06) measured the Behringer NX3000D at about 400 W per channel into 4 Ω, falling to 268 W at 20 Hz, against Behringer's 900 W rating. That is the amp ChatGPT ranked first as 'best value for powerful subs'. On the same test bench, the Crown XLS1002 went onto ASR's recommended list 'for driving subwoofers'.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited B&H compare pages (NX3000D vs XLS1002/EPQ304/A800 and NX3000D vs XLS1502) and the ChurchSoundCalc top result. The B&H pages returned HTTP 403 when I tried to open them. They are retailer compare tables, so they would carry maker ratings, and ChatGPT's answer repeats the '1,500-watt' maker figure. ChurchSoundCalc states 'We did not test these products in person' and lists only maker ratings (NX3000D 1,500 W/ch at 4 Ω; XLS1002 350 W/ch at 4 Ω). None of these pages gives a measured figure, and none gives power at subwoofer frequencies.
decides: This undercuts ChatGPT's top pick. At 20 Hz, where a passive sub needs the power, Amir measured the NX3000D at 268 W per channel, about 30% of its 900 W/ch 4 Ω rating. The same reviewer measured the Crown XLS1502 at about 336 W at 0.008% distortion. He recommended both the XLS1002 and the XLS1502 for subwoofer duty, and he faulted the NX3000D's fan for running at full speed from power-up. So the Crown is the better-sourced pick, and the NX3000D's '1,500 W' headline should not decide a purchase. I found no measurements for the Dayton SPA250DSP or the Fosi M03, so on this angle neither can be ranked against the rack amps.

findings.label: Measured power at 20 Hz, 4 Ω (ASR, amirm)
findings.value: 268 W per channel (Behringer rating: 900 W per channel at 4 Ω)
findings.source_title: Behringer NX3000D Pro DSP Amplifier Review | Audio Science Review
findings.note: Review posted 2020-07-06. Quote: 'it is disappointing to see it dip so low to just 268 watts for an amplifier rated at "900 watts."' 268/900 = 30% of rating. Amir drives both channels in his power tests.

findings.label: Measured full-band power, 4 Ω, both channels driven (ASR, amirm)
findings.source_title: Behringer NX3000D Pro DSP Amplifier Review | Audio Science Review
findings.note: Quote: '400 watts is lots of power in such a cheap package' and 'the rated power numbers are a fantasy unless they are measured for one channel driven, not two as I do.' Exact figures are in chart images. He also wrote that the fan 'is not temperature sensitive and wails away upon power up', with no dB figure given.

findings.label: ASR verdict for subwoofer use (amirm)
findings.value: Recommended 'for non-critical applications or for driving subwoofers'. SINAD 'slightly below the average of all amps tested'. One channel measured 'much worse than the other'.
findings.source_title: Crown XLS1002 Pro Amplifier Review | Audio Science Review
findings.note: Review posted 2020-09-25. The numeric SINAD and power figures are only in chart images. Fan: 'none came on that I could hear above the sound of my PC during testing.' He also noted that the limiter keeps burst power from rising above continuous power.

findings.label: Measured power, 4 Ω (from ASR charts, relayed by a forum member)
findings.value: about 340 W at 1% THD; about 280 W at the clipping 'elbow' (Crown rating: 350 W/ch at 4 Ω)
findings.source_title: Crown XLS1002 Pro Amplifier Review, page 2 | Audio Science Review
findings.note: Secondhand: member MediumRare, post #31 on 2020-09-25, wrote 'Amir measured 340 into 4 ohms at 1% THD and 280 at the elbow'. I could not read the chart images to confirm. In the same thread a commenter wrote that the NX3000D 'clocked in at a SINAD of 68 dB'. That is also secondhand, so I left it out as a finding.

findings.label: Measured power and SINAD, 4 Ω (ASR, amirm)
findings.value: about 336 W at 0.008% distortion; SINAD 75 dB at 5 W (Crown rating: 525 W/ch at 4 Ω)
findings.source_title: Review and Measurements of Crown XLS 1502 Amp | Audio Science Review
findings.note: Review posted 2019-01-06. Amir says 336 W understates the maximum because his data lacked points near clipping. He saw 'some roll off at 20 Hz' in the frequency response and concluded the amp's 'best use would be as a subwoofer amplifier'. In a soak test near 50 W the fan 'barely came on' and was 'very quiet'.

unsourced: Measured output for the Dayton Audio SPA250DSP. I searched for ASR, Audioholics and named-reviewer bench tests and found only maker/retailer ratings (250 W RMS at 4 Ω) and one anonymous eBay opinion.
Measured output for the Fosi Audio M03 on its bundled 32 V / 5 A supply. I searched ASR and general reviews and found no bench test, only Fosi's rating (about 150 W at 4 Ω) and buyer comments.
Numeric SINAD and watt figures for the Crown XLS1002 from Amir's own text. They are only in chart images I could not read. The 340 W / 280 W figures come from a forum member.
Power at 20 Hz and in bridged mode for the Crown XLS1002 and XLS1502. Neither ASR review reports it.
What the two cited B&H compare pages contain. Both returned HTTP 403 when I tried to open them, so I judged them from their titles and from ChatGPT's answer.
